observations:
Torah #161 is a compressed two-line aphorism with a total of 5 bechina-identified concept nodes across 2 packages. The new-package threshold requires 3 or more bechina-connected concepts forming an independent domain not already captured by the existing package structure. No such independent domain exists in this Torah.

The two packages proposed in torah_161_packages.json exhaust the bechina-language content of the teaching:
  Package 1 (מַחֲלֹקֶת וּמַיִם — neutral): 3 nodes, all expressing the same water/force/conflict domain
  Package 2 (אָדָם וְעֵץ הַשָּׂדֶה — good): 2 nodes, the subject of elevation

The teaching's argumentative structure is a single two-move sequence:
  [Pkg 2: good — the elevated person] ← eitza ← [Pkg 1: neutral — conflict as water]

There is no third thematic domain in the source text. The concept of הַגְבָּהָה/הֲרָמָה (elevation) functions as the eitza-verb connecting the two packages, not as an independent bechina cluster. No additional concepts receive bechina-identification language ('בְּחִינַת', 'נִקְרָא', 'הַיְנוּ', 'כִּי' in an identity-asserting usage) beyond those already assigned to the two packages.

The absence of a third package is consistent with the teaching's genre (compressed aphorism) and its extreme brevity (approximately 80 words). Torah #161 presents a single structural insight — conflict IS water, the person IS a tree, water raises trees — and stops there. Unlike the longer Torahs in Likutey Moharan, which develop multi-stage arguments with several distinct conceptual domains, this Torah states its paradox and grounds it in one physical analogy and one proof-text. The two-package structure reflects this intentional minimalism.

The good/evil mirror structure is absent from this Torah: the Rebbe does not describe an evil counterpart to the elevation-through-conflict teaching. There is no evil מַחֲלֹקֶת cluster (the negative function of conflict — its destructive, division-causing aspect) developed in bechina language. The paradox of the teaching depends precisely on presenting machloket monolithically as the elevating force, without developing its destructive dimension as a separate bechina domain.
